title: C: drive is full, it keeps filling up even though I clean it regularly
description: There's 5 GB left on the C: drive. I run Disk Cleanup, but it's full again after 2-3 days.

worklogs.description: Analyzed with WinDirStat, identified %temp% (24 GB) and old .iso backups (45 GB).
Enabled OneDrive Files On-Demand, freed up 80 GB of local cache.
Checked the service inventory, a 512 GB SSD upgrade is in stock.
Service appointment scheduled and SSD upgrade performed; data migrated.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: This problem has been going on for 6 months, I keep fixing it temporarily but it comes back every time. The computer is very slow, please do something permanent.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: I understand, that must be very frustrating. Let's get the full picture first, then I'll recommend a solution that's both fast and permanent. We'll run a tool to see the big areas: 'winget install WinDirStat' (run it → accept). After it's installed, open it and analyze C:\, then could you send me a screenshot of the result?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: WinDirStat ran, I've attached a screenshot. The biggest: AppData\Local\Temp 24 GB, then D:\ISOs 45 GB (old Windows isos). Then Outlook OST 8 GB.

comments.author: agent
comments.message:
Excellent diagnosis. The %temp% folder is 24 GB! The OS normally cleans it, but something is blocking it. The old .iso files aren't needed anymore either. As a temporary fix, let's do these steps now:
1) Win+R → %temp% → Select all files → Delete (skip the ones in use)
2) Delete the .iso files in D:\ISOs (if you really need them, let's move them to the file share)
3) Enable OneDrive Files On-Demand
These steps will free up ~80 GB. Can you do them?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: I did all of it! C: now has 90 GB free. It's a huge difference, the computer is 2x faster. But what if it fills up again in 6 months?

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Glad to hear it! For a permanent fix: your device has a 256 GB SSD. For developers like you, that's now too small. There's a 512 GB SSD in the service inventory, I'll get approval. The process is as follows: 1) My IT manager approves within 1 day, 2) You drop off the device with me for a day, 3) The data is cloned (3-4 hours), 4) You get the computer back. When works for you?

comments.author: customer
comments.message: On Fridays I work from home. Could I drop it off Thursday evening and pick it up end of Friday/Monday morning?

comments.author: agent
comments.message: Perfect plan. I'll take it Thursday at 17:00, and it'll be ready at your desk Monday at 09:00. There won't be any data loss — I'll use the disk clone method. I've reserved the appointment for this Thursday. You'll be comfortable now with the temporary fix, and the permanent fix will be ready next week.

comments.author: customer
comments.message: Great, I'm very happy. See you Thursday.

comments.author: agent
comments.message: SSD upgrade appointment recorded (inventory slot #SU-2024-019). I'll use Macrium Reflect for the clone. After the work, I'll wait for the user's approval to close the ticket.

resolutionNote: Short-term: cleaned up %temp% (24 GB) and old .isos (45 GB) with WinDirStat, enabled OneDrive Files On-Demand → ~90 GB freed. Permanent: 256 GB → 512 GB SSD upgrade completed in the Thursday-Monday window, data transferred via clone. User is satisfied with both solutions.

csat.comment: Both an immediate and a permanent solution, plus a very detailed explanation. The process was managed very well.
